q: What is the chemical symbol for water?
fact: Water is made of two hydrogen atoms and one oxygen atom.

q: What force pulls objects toward the Earth?
fact: Gravity is the force that gives weight to objects and keeps us on the ground.

q: How many bones are there in an adult human body?
fact: Babies are born with about 300 bones, but many fuse together as they grow, leaving 206 in adults.

q: Which gas do plants absorb from the air for photosynthesis?
fact: Plants use carbon dioxide, water, and sunlight to make their own food.

q: At sea level, at what temperature does water boil in Celsius?
fact: At standard sea-level pressure, pure water boils at exactly 100 degrees Celsius.

q: Which organ pumps blood around the human body?
fact: The human heart beats about 100,000 times every day.

q: What is the center of an atom called?
fact: The nucleus contains protons and neutrons and holds nearly all of an atom's mass.

q: What sweet substance do bees produce?
fact: A single bee produces only about one-twelfth of a teaspoon of honey in its lifetime.

q: What is the solid form of water called?
fact: Ice is less dense than liquid water, which is why ice cubes float.

q: Which gas do humans need to breathe in to survive?
fact: Humans use oxygen to convert food into energy in their cells.

q: What is the largest organ of the human body?
fact: An adult's skin covers an area of about two square meters.

q: What does a caterpillar change into?
fact: This transformation is called metamorphosis and can take weeks to complete.

q: Which part of a plant makes most of its food?
fact: Leaves contain chlorophyll, the green pigment that captures sunlight.

q: What are animals that eat only plants called?
fact: Cows, rabbits, and deer are all herbivores.

q: How many legs does an insect have?
fact: All insects have six legs and three main body parts.

q: Which gas is used to fill balloons so they float?
fact: Helium is lighter than air, so helium balloons rise.

q: What is the chemical formula for table salt?
fact: Table salt is sodium chloride: one sodium atom bonded to one chlorine atom.

q: Which sense do you mainly use with your eyes?
fact: The human eye can distinguish roughly ten million different colors.

q: How many bones does an adult human have?
fact: Babies are born with about 300 bones, many of which fuse as they grow.

q: What is the chemical symbol for gold?
fact: Au comes from aurum, the Latin word for gold.

q: What is the pH of a neutral solution?
fact: Pure water is neutral with a pH of 7 at room temperature.

q: What is the standard unit of force?
fact: The newton is named after Sir Isaac Newton.

q: What shape describes the structure of DNA?
fact: James Watson and Francis Crick described the double helix structure in 1953.

q: About how fast does light travel in a vacuum?
fact: Light from the Sun takes about eight minutes to reach Earth.

q: Which blood cells carry oxygen around the body?
fact: Red blood cells get their color from hemoglobin, which binds oxygen.

q: What force resists motion between two surfaces touching each other?
fact: Friction is why a sliding box eventually comes to a stop.

q: What is the chemical symbol for sodium?
fact: Na comes from natrium, the Latin name for sodium.

q: Which organ produces insulin in the human body?
fact: Insulin helps control the level of sugar in the blood.

q: What is the process called when water vapor cools and becomes liquid?
fact: Condensation is why dew forms on grass on cool mornings.

q: Which gas makes up most of Earth's atmosphere?
fact: Nitrogen makes up about 78 percent of Earth's atmosphere.

q: Which acid gives lemons their sour taste?
fact: Citric acid is also found in oranges, limes, and grapefruits.

q: How many chromosomes do humans normally have in each cell?
fact: Human chromosomes are arranged in 23 pairs.

q: What is the chemical symbol for iron?
fact: Fe comes from ferrum, the Latin word for iron.

q: What is known as the powerhouse of the cell?
fact: Mitochondria produce most of a cell's energy in the form of ATP.

q: What is the hardest naturally occurring substance on Earth?
fact: Diamonds are made of carbon atoms arranged in a very strong crystal structure.

q: What is Avogadro's number, approximately?
fact: Avogadro's number is the number of particles in one mole of a substance.

q: Which blood type is known as the universal donor?
fact: O negative blood can be given to people of almost any blood type in emergencies.

q: Which enzyme begins the digestion of starch in the mouth?
fact: Salivary amylase starts breaking down starches before food reaches the stomach.

q: What is the chemical symbol for antimony?
fact: Sb comes from stibium, the Latin name for antimony.

q: Which cell structure is the main site of protein synthesis?
fact: Ribosomes build proteins by following instructions from messenger RNA.

q: Who proposed the theory of evolution by natural selection?
fact: Darwin published his theory in On the Origin of Species in 1859.

q: What is the approximate pH of healthy human blood?
fact: The body keeps blood pH tightly controlled between about 7.35 and 7.45.

q: After oxygen, what is the second most abundant element in the human body by mass?
fact: Carbon forms the backbone of proteins, fats, and carbohydrates in the body.

q: Which subatomic particle has a negative electric charge?
fact: Electrons are far lighter than protons and neutrons.

q: Which component of blood helps it to clot?
fact: Platelets rush to the site of a cut and stick together to plug the wound.
